proofs.proof_tex:
For a fixed connected simple graph \(H\), choosing \(X_i\) from the factor indexed by \(\{i,j\}\) is the same as orienting that edge toward \(i\). Consequently \(c_H(r)\) is exactly the number of orientations of \(H\) with indegree vector \(r\). Only finitely many labeled simple graphs on at most \(N\) vertices and finitely many orientations of each graph occur, so the maximum defining \(\vartheta_{N,g}\) is finite. Enlarging \(N\) or \(g\) enlarges the feasible collection, proving monotonicity.

Fix a spanning tree \(S\) of \(H\), write \(b=|V(H)|\), and put \(h=g(H)\). There are
\[
 |E(H)\setminus E(S)|=|E(H)|-(b-1)=h
\]
non-tree edges. For a prescribed indegree vector \(r\), fix orientations of those \(h\) edges. There is at most one compatible orientation of \(S\): at a leaf of the current tree, the prescribed residual indegree forces the orientation of its unique remaining tree edge, after which that leaf may be deleted. Induction on the number of tree vertices proves uniqueness. Therefore
\[
 c_H(r)\leq 2^h\leq 2^g.
\tag{1}
\]
The fixed-edge completion proved in \(\mathrm{lem:tournament\mbox{-}score\mbox{-}fiber\mbox{-}ceiling}\) also gives \(c_H(r)\leq\tau_N\) whenever \(b\leq N\). Taking the maximum over \(H,r\) proves
\[
 \vartheta_{N,g}\leq\min\{2^g,\tau_N\}.
\tag{2}
\]

We next prove the exact maximality threshold. If \(g=0\), the included one-vertex graph gives \(\vartheta_{N,0}\geq1=2^0\), which combines with (1); because \(N\geq1=2g+1\), the asserted equivalence holds. Now let \(g\geq1\). For sufficiency, form a bouquet of \(g\) triangles by taking a central vertex \(z\), two new vertices \(u_i,v_i\) for each \(1\leq i\leq g\), and the three edges
\[
 \{z,u_i\},\qquad \{u_i,v_i\},\qquad \{v_i,z\}
\]
for each \(i\). This connected simple graph has \(2g+1\) vertices, \(3g\) edges, and hence cyclomatic number
\[
 3g-(2g+1)+1=g.
\]
Orient each triangle as either of its two directed cycles. Every such choice has indegree \(g\) at \(z\) and indegree one at every \(u_i,v_i\). The choices are independent across triangles, so for
\[
 r_z=g,\qquad r_{u_i}=r_{v_i}=1
\]
the score fiber contains \(2^g\) orientations. Thus \(\vartheta_{N,g}\geq2^g\) when \(N\geq2g+1\), and (1) proves equality.

For necessity, suppose \(\vartheta_{N,g}=2^g\). Finiteness shows that some feasible connected simple graph \(H\) on \(b\leq N\) vertices and some \(r\) attain this maximum. If \(h=g(H)\), then (1) gives
\[
 2^g=c_H(r)\leq2^h\leq2^g,
\]
so \(h=g\), and all \(2^h\) orientations of the cotree \(E(H)\setminus E(S)\) extend to orientations in the score fiber: the restriction map from the score fiber to the \(2^h\) cotree orientations is injective by the tree-uniqueness argument and has equally large domain and codomain.

We make the resulting constraint explicit. Give every tree edge \(s\) ordered endpoints \((a_s,b_s)\), and let \(y_s=1\) mean that \(s\) is oriented toward \(b_s\), while \(y_s=0\) means that it is oriented toward \(a_s\). Similarly order the cotree edges \(f_j\), \(1\leq j\leq h\), and encode their orientations by \(x_j\in\{0,1\}\). Delete one vertex row from the oriented incidence matrix of \(S\), obtaining a square matrix \(Q\), and let \(C\) be the correspondingly reduced incidence matrix of the cotree. Since \(S\) is a tree, leaf elimination makes \(Q\) invertible. The prescribed-indegree equations have the form
\[
 Qy=\beta-Cx,
 \qquad
 y(x)=Q^{-1}\beta-Q^{-1}Cx
\tag{3}
\]
for a constant vector \(\beta\) determined by \(r\) and the chosen endpoint orders.

For the cotree edge \(f_j\), let \(P_j\) be the unique path in \(S\) joining its endpoints. The unique solution of the incidence equation for the \(j\)-th column of \(C\) is unit flow along \(P_j\); hence the \(j\)-th column of \(Q^{-1}C\) is zero off \(P_j\) and is \(1\) or \(-1\) on every edge of \(P_j\), with the sign determined by the endpoint orders. Consequently each coordinate in (3) is an affine function
\[
 y_s(x)=\alpha_s+\sum_{j:s\in P_j}\epsilon_{sj}x_j,
 \qquad \epsilon_{sj}\in\{-1,1\}.
\tag{4}
\]
Every \(x\in\{0,1\}^h\) extends, so \(y_s(x)\in\{0,1\}\) on the full Boolean cube. The range diameter of the affine function in (4) on that cube is
\[
 \max_x y_s(x)-\min_x y_s(x)
 =\sum_{j:s\in P_j}|\epsilon_{sj}|.
\tag{5}
\]
Its left side is at most one. Thus every tree edge belongs to at most one of \(P_1,\ldots,P_g\); these fundamental-cycle paths are pairwise edge-disjoint. Because \(H\) is simple and \(f_j\notin E(S)\), the path \(P_j\) cannot have length one, for that would make its unique tree edge parallel to \(f_j\). Therefore \(|P_j|\geq2\), and edge-disjointness gives
\[
 b-1=|E(S)|\geq\sum_{j=1}^{g}|P_j|\geq2g.
\]
Since \(b\leq N\), necessarily \(N\geq2g+1\). Together with the bouquet construction this proves
\[
 \vartheta_{N,g}=2^g\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad N\geq2g+1.
\tag{6}
\]

It remains to certify the five-vertex values. Given a labeled graph \(H\) with lexicographically ordered edges \(e_j=\{u_j,v_j\}\), define
\[
 A_{H,0}(r)=\mathbf 1\{r=0\},
 \qquad
 A_{H,j}(r)=A_{H,j-1}(r-\mathbf e_{u_j})
             +A_{H,j-1}(r-\mathbf e_{v_j}),
\tag{7}
\]
where a term with a negative coordinate is zero. Expanding one factor at a time proves by induction that
\[
 A_{H,|E(H)|}(r)=c_H(r).
\tag{8}
\]
Put \(\mu(H)=\max_r c_H(r)\), and let \(N_{b,m}(s)\) be the number of connected labeled graphs on \([b]\) with \(m\) edges and \(\mu(H)=s\). Applying the additions in (7) to every subset of the at most ten possible edges gives the following finite audit table; within a row, \(N(s)\) abbreviates \(N_{b,m}(s)\), and a blank entry is zero:
\[
\begin{array}{c|c|l|c}
b&m&\{s:N_{b,m}(s)\ne0\}&\sum_sN_{b,m}(s)\\ \hline
1&0&N(1)=1&1\\
2&1&N(1)=1&1\\
3&2&N(1)=3&3\\
3&3&N(2)=1&1\\
4&3&N(1)=16&16\\
4&4&N(2)=15&15\\
4&5&N(3)=6&6\\
4&6&N(4)=1&1\\
5&4&N(1)=125&125\\
5&5&N(2)=222&222\\
5&6&N(3)=190,\ N(4)=15&205\\
5&7&N(4)=50,\ N(5)=60,\ N(6)=10&120\\
5&8&N(7)=15,\ N(8)=30&45\\
5&9&N(12)=10&10\\
5&10&N(24)=1&1
\end{array}
\tag{9}
\]
This table is independently checkable without graph-isomorphism choices: scan the edge subsets in lexicographic order, reject a subset unless a search from vertex \(1\) reaches all \(b\) vertices, and use (7). As an arithmetic checksum, if \(a_{b,m}=\sum_sN_{b,m}(s)\), decomposition by the connected component containing vertex \(1\) gives
\[
 a_{1,0}=1,
 \qquad
 a_{b,m}=\binom{\binom b2}{m}
 -\sum_{q=1}^{b-1}\binom{b-1}{q-1}
   \sum_{\ell=0}^{m}a_{q,\ell}
   \binom{\binom{b-q}{2}}{m-\ell}.
\tag{10}
\]
Substitution in (10) gives exactly the last column of (9).

The maxima in the seven five-vertex rows are attained explicitly. Let
\[
 S_0=\{12,13,14,15\},
\]
and, for \(0\leq h\leq6\), let \(H_h\) have edge set \(S_0\cup A_h\), where the following table also gives a score vector whose coefficient is maximal:
\[
\begin{array}{c|l|c|c}
h&A_h&r&c_{H_h}(r)\\ \hline
0&\varnothing&(4,0,0,0,0)&1\\
1&\{23\}&(3,1,1,0,0)&2\\
2&\{25,34\}&(2,1,1,1,1)&4\\
3&\{23,24,25\}&(2,2,1,1,1)&6\\
4&\{23,24,25,34\}&(2,2,2,1,1)&8\\
5&\{23,24,25,34,35\}&(2,2,2,2,1)&12\\
6&\{23,24,25,34,35,45\}&(2,2,2,2,2)&24
\end{array}
\tag{11}
\]
Each coefficient in (11) follows by the same recurrence (7), after the four star edges have been processed. Since a connected graph with \(b\) vertices and \(m\) edges has cyclomatic number \(m-b+1\), (9) supplies the upper bounds and (11) supplies matching lower bounds for every \(0\leq g\leq6\). Hence
\[
 (\vartheta_{5,g})_{g=0}^{6}=(1,2,4,6,8,12,24).
\]
Finally a simple graph on at most five vertices has cyclomatic number at most
\[
 \binom52-5+1=6.
\]
Thus increasing \(g\) beyond six adds no feasible graph, and \(\vartheta_{5,g}=24\) for every \(g\geq6\).

added_lemmas.statement:
For every pair of integers \(N\geq1\) and \(g\geq0\), the joint orientation frontier attains its spanning-tree bound exactly if and only if
\[
 \vartheta_{N,g}=2^g
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 N\geq2g+1.
\]
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
The forward implication in the displayed equivalence is proved by the deleted-incidence argument below, and the reverse implication is the triangle-bouquet construction in \(\mathrm{lem:joint\mbox{-}orientation\mbox{-}frontier}\). For \(g=0\), the definition assumes \(N\geq1=2g+1\), while the one-vertex graph and the universal bound give \(\vartheta_{N,0}=1\).

Let \(g\geq1\) and suppose \(\vartheta_{N,g}=2^g\). By finiteness and the bound in \(\mathrm{lem:joint\mbox{-}orientation\mbox{-}frontier}\), an attaining pair \((H,r)\) must have cyclomatic number exactly \(g\), and restriction to the cotree of any spanning tree \(S\) bijects its score fiber with all \(2^g\) cotree orientations. Indeed, restriction is injective because successive leaf deletion uniquely determines any compatible orientation of \(S\).

Delete one row from the oriented incidence matrix of \(S\), call the resulting invertible matrix \(Q\), and let \(C\) be the reduced incidence matrix of the cotree. If \(x\in\{0,1\}^g\) records the cotree orientations and \(y\) the tree orientations, the prescribed-indegree equations give
\[
 y(x)=Q^{-1}\beta-Q^{-1}Cx.
\]
For a cotree edge \(f_j\), the corresponding column of \(Q^{-1}C\) is the signed unit flow along the unique tree path \(P_j\) joining its endpoints. Hence every coordinate of \(y\) is affine on the full Boolean cube, with a coefficient of absolute value one for precisely those \(j\) whose path \(P_j\) uses that tree edge. Since all cotree choices extend, each such affine coordinate is always in \(\{0,1\}\). Its range diameter equals the sum of the absolute values of its coefficients and is at most one. Thus \(P_1,\ldots,P_g\) are pairwise edge-disjoint. Simplicity forces \(|P_j|\geq2\), because a length-one path would duplicate \(f_j\). Therefore
\[
 N-1\geq |E(S)|\geq\sum_{j=1}^g|P_j|\geq2g,
\]
which gives \(N\geq2g+1\). This proves necessity and completes the equivalence.

prose_updates.tldr: Adding parents to a supplied rooted tree creates finite ambiguity measured here by the single-coordinate complex degree \(D_k(n)\), not by whole-fiber cardinality or real root count. For \(n\geq4\), the paper proves \(2^{\min\{k+1,\lfloor(n-2)/2\rfloor\}}\leq D_k(n)\leq\vartheta_{n-1,k+1}\leq\min\{2^{k+1},\tau_{n-1}\}\). The combinatorial maximum satisfies the exact threshold \(\vartheta_{N,g}=2^g\) if and only if \(N\geq2g+1\), and the SEM frontier satisfies \(D_k(n)=2^{k+1}\) if and only if \(n\geq2k+4\). Hence throughout the remaining positive-excess strip \(n\geq6\) and \(n<2k+4\), the frontier is strictly below \(2^{k+1}\), although its exact value remains open. The exact five-vertex orientation recurrence gives \((1,2,4,6,8,12,24)\) and the stated six-vertex upper bounds. The zero-excess dispatcher retains the complete published \(1/2/\infty\) classification and finite expressions; at positive excess it retains the existing efficiently reportable size-binomial bound. Exact polynomials, exceptional sets, real lifting, and regular inference are asserted only conditional on a supplied valid source-prime chart and successful output.

project_justification.fill: The paper proves the coupled projection-aware envelope \(2^{\min\{k+1,\lfloor(n-2)/2\rfloor\}}\leq D_k(n)\leq\vartheta_{n-1,k+1}\leq\min\{2^{k+1},\tau_{n-1}\}\) for \(n\geq4\). A deleted-incidence argument and a triangle-bouquet construction give the exact combinatorial threshold \(\vartheta_{N,g}=2^g\) if and only if \(N\geq2g+1\). Combined with the one-sink SEM construction, this yields the sharp maximality threshold \(D_k(n)=2^{k+1}\) if and only if \(n\geq2k+4\) for every admissible \((n,k)\). Thus the unresolved positive-excess strip is proved strictly submaximal, while its exact values remain open. The paper also gives the exact five-vertex orientation recurrence, the resulting six-vertex upper row, the inherited all-size lower envelope, and the exact \(n\leq5\) coordinate-degree frontier. It supplies an unconditional randomized Jacobian-rank tag, retains the complete published tree-case output at \(k=0\), and proves geometric-resolution, exceptional-set, real-lifting, and regular-inference results only conditional on a supplied valid source-prime chart and successful output.

sampling_model.design: The identification layer uses the exact population covariance of a known recursive Gaussian mixed graph and distinguishes the queried-coordinate field degree from whole-fiber size and real root count. Across the admissible graph classes, maximal finite ambiguity \(2^{k+1}\) occurs if and only if \(n\geq2k+4\); below that threshold the degree is strictly smaller, with exact values still open in the remaining positive-excess strip. The unconditional symbolic layer returns an algebraic-versus-transcendental queried-coordinate tag. The estimation layer is available at fixed \(G,n\) only conditional on a supplied valid source-prime chart and successful finite eliminant and certificate output.

prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: For \(k>0\), \(n\geq6\), and \(n<2k+4\), the exact frontier remains open but now satisfies the strict chain \(2^{\min\{k+1,\lfloor(n-2)/2\rfloor\}}\leq D_k(n)\leq\vartheta_{n-1,k+1}<2^{k+1}\). The quantity \(\vartheta_{n-1,k+1}\) is a combinatorial upper bound; equality with the SEM frontier is not asserted because branches may be lost through forced covariance relations, exact localization, affine dehomogenization, or projective infinity. The five-vertex orientation recurrence gives the six-vertex bounds \(6,8,12,24\) for \(k=2,3,4,\geq5\), respectively, but no attaining SEM family is asserted. The unconditional fixed-parameter dispatcher retains the efficiently explicit size-binomial bound because no uniform exact computation and certificate for \(\vartheta_{n-1,k+1}\) within its runtime is supplied. The exhaustive five-node orbit census remains a secondary regression and coordinate-census question because the cubic and quartic base cases and the entire \(n\leq5\) frontier are fixed. Independently, the quadratic core does not construct a reduced local presentation of the embedded source prime or bounded rational-circuit descent over \(K_G\). Conditional on a supplied valid source-prime chart and successful output, the exceptional-set theorem, real-root-lifting theorem, regular-cell lemma, derived root-separation lemma, regular finite-set inference theorem, and singleton inference proposition hold. No chart-free statistical theorem is asserted. Coordinate localization is never promoted to equality of full fibers, real roots are never equated with real supported lifts, and local rank is not used to assert real uniqueness.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The paper proves the full frontier through five vertices, the all-size lower envelope, and the coupled upper inequality \(D_k(n)\leq\vartheta_{n-1,k+1}\leq\min\{2^{k+1},\tau_{n-1}\}\). It proves \(\vartheta_{N,g}=2^g\) if and only if \(N\geq2g+1\) and, using the separate one-sink construction, \(D_k(n)=2^{k+1}\) if and only if \(n\geq2k+4\). Therefore the remaining positive-excess strip is strictly submaximal, but its exact frontier is not determined. The recurrence \((\vartheta_{5,g})_{g=0}^{6}=(1,2,4,6,8,12,24)\) yields \(D_2(6)\leq6\), \(D_3(6)\leq8\), \(D_4(6)\leq12\), and \(D_k(6)\leq24\) for admissible \(k\geq5\), alongside \(D_0(6)=2\) and \(D_1(6)=4\). Unconditionally, the dispatcher returns the complete published \(1/2/\infty\) classification and finite \(\operatorname{FASTP}\) expressions on \(\mathcal G_{n,0}\). For \(|D\setminus T|>0\), it returns only a randomized algebraic-versus-transcendental tag, a rank or dominance certificate, and the efficiently available bound \(d_e(G)\leq2^{\min\{|D|-n+2,\binom{n-2}{2}\}}\); it does not compute \(\vartheta_{n-1,k+1}\), \(d_e(G)\), \(p_e\), \(\mathcal Q_{G,e}\), or \(h_{G,e}\) on the algebraic branch. Conditional on a supplied valid source-prime chart and successful output, the geometric-resolution theorem returns the exact finite objects with its stated straight-line-program and intermediate-degree dependence, and the exceptional-set, real-lifting, and regular-inference results hold. No discriminant-uniform inference, automatic branch selection, or all-singular-covariance guarantee is claimed, and positive definiteness of recovered noise follows only after a complete real supported lift by congruence.

proofs.proof_tex:
Put \(d=k+1\) and \(N=2d+2=2k+4\).  We first treat the graph on exactly \(N\) vertices.  In the graph of \(\mathrm{def:attaining\mbox{-}family}\), the directed edges are
\[
 0\to P_i,\qquad 0\to Q_i,\qquad P_i\to h
 \quad(1\leq i\leq d).
\]
The supplied arborescence consists of the first \(2d\) edges and \(P_1\to h\).  Hence
\[
 |T|=2d+1=N-1,\qquad
 D\setminus T=\{P_i\to h:2\leq i\leq d\},\qquad
 |D\setminus T|=d-1=k.                                      \tag{1}
\]
Every nonroot vertex has exactly one incoming edge in \(T\), every vertex is reached from \(0\), and
\[
 0,P_1,Q_1,\ldots,P_d,Q_d,h
\]
is a topological order.  Thus the acyclicity and arborescence conditions in \(\mathrm{def:graph\mbox{-}class}\) hold, and (1) proves
\[
 (G^{\star}_{k,N},T,e^{\star})\in\mathcal G_{N,k}.             \tag{2}
\]

We now construct a regular covariance fiber.  Choose positive rational numbers \(h_i\) and rational numbers \(b_i\) such that
\[
 b_i^2>4h_i\qquad(1\leq i\leq d),
\]
and set \(H_0=\operatorname{diag}(h_1,\ldots,h_d)\).  Choose a rational symmetric positive-definite matrix \(H\), sufficiently close to \(H_0\), with diagonal \((h_1,\ldots,h_d)\); a further generic restriction on its off-diagonal entries will be imposed below.  In the vertex order \((0,P_1,\ldots,P_d,Q_1,\ldots,Q_d,h)\), define
\[
 \Sigma^{\star}=
 \begin{pmatrix}
  1&0&0&1\\
  0&H&H&0\\
  0&H&C_0I_d&b\\
  1&0&b^{\mathsf T}&M
 \end{pmatrix},
 \qquad b=(b_1,\ldots,b_d)^{\mathsf T}.                       \tag{3}
\]
Choose rational \(C_0\) so that \(C_0I_d-H\succ0\).  Since \(H\succ0\), the Schur complement of \(H\) in the \((P,Q)\)-principal block of (3) is
\[
 C_0I_d-HH^{-1}H=C_0I_d-H\succ0.
\]
Thus that principal block is positive definite.  The \(0\)-coordinate is independent of the \((P,Q)\)-block, and choosing rational \(M\) larger than the final Schur-complement threshold therefore gives
\[
 Sigma^{\star}\succ0.                                       \tag{4}
\]

Write
\[
 a_i=\lambda_{0P_i},\qquad c_i=\lambda_{0Q_i},\qquad
 z_i=\lambda_{P_i h},\qquad z=(z_1,\ldots,z_d)^{\mathsf T},
 \qquad x=-Hz.
\]
The only absent bidirected pairs are \(P_i\leftrightarrow Q_i\), \(P_i\leftrightarrow h\), and \(Q_i\leftrightarrow h\), for \(1\leq i\leq d\).  Substitution of (3) into the residual formula defining \(F_{ij}\) gives, respectively,
\[
 0=h_i+a_ic_i,\qquad
 0=-a_i-(Hz)_i,\qquad
 0=b_i-c_i-(Hz)_i.                                            \tag{5}
\]
Because \(H\) is positive definite and hence invertible, (5) is equivalent to
\[
 a_i=x_i,\qquad c_i=x_i+b_i,\qquad
 x_i^2+b_ix_i+h_i=0\quad(1\leq i\leq d),
 \qquad z=-H^{-1}x.                                          \tag{6}
\]
The discriminant of the \(i\)-th quadratic is \(b_i^2-4h_i>0\).  Consequently (6) has exactly \(2^d\) real solutions.  Under the invertible linear change \(z\mapsto x=-Hz\), the Jacobian of the \(3d\) equations in (5), with respect to \((a,c,z)\), is nonsingular precisely when
\[
 det(H)\prod_{i=1}^d(2x_i+b_i)\ne0.                          \tag{7}
\]
Indeed, for each \(i\), the determinant of the three corresponding equations in \((a_i,c_i,x_i)\) is, up to sign, \(a_i+c_i=2x_i+b_i\), and at a solution
\[
 (2x_i+b_i)^2=b_i^2-4h_i>0.
\]
Thus all \(2^d\) solutions are reduced.  For each solution define
\[
 \Omega=(I_N-\Lambda)^{\mathsf T}\Sigma^{\star}(I_N-\Lambda). \tag{8}
\]
Equations (5) say exactly that every required missing off-diagonal entry of \(\Omega\) is zero.  The displayed topological order makes \(I_N-\Lambda\) unit triangular and therefore invertible.  Equation (4) and congruence in (8) imply \(\Omega\succ0\).  Hence every point in (6) is a real supported positive-definite source lift of the same covariance.

It remains to make the queried coordinate distinguish the \(2^d\) lifts.  At \(H=H_0\), two branches whose first coordinates differ have distinct values \(z_1=-x_1/h_1\).  If \(x\ne x'\) have the same first coordinate, choose \(j>1\) with \(x_j\ne x'_j\) and put \(H(s)=H_0+s(E_{1j}+E_{j1})\).  Differentiating \(-H(s)^{-1}x\) at zero gives
\[
 \left.\frac{d}{ds}\{z_1(x)-z_1(x')\}\right|_{s=0}
   =\frac{x_j-x'_j}{h_1h_j}\ne0.                              \tag{9}
\]
Thus, for every pair of distinct branches, equality of their \(z_1\)-values is a proper algebraic condition on the off-diagonal entries of \(H\).  There are finitely many pairs.  A finite union of proper algebraic subsets cannot contain a Euclidean neighborhood of \(H_0\), and rational matrices are dense in that neighborhood.  We may therefore choose the rational positive-definite \(H\) in (3) outside this union.  For that choice the \(2^d\) values of
\[
 z_1=\lambda_{e^{\star}}
\]
are pairwise distinct.

We next pass from this regular special fiber to the generic field degree.  There are \(3d\) directed coordinates and exactly \(3d\) absent bidirected pairs.  Because every other pair is bidirected,
\[
 |D|+|B|+|V|
 =3d+\left(\binom N2-3d\right)+N
 =\frac{N(N+1)}2=:M_0.                                      \tag{10}
\]
Perturb all \(M_0\) independent entries of \(\Sigma^{\star}\) by algebraically independent variables \(\xi\).  At any one of the reduced points \(v_0=(a,c,z)\), seek a formal solution
\[
 v(\xi)=v_0+\sum_{r\geq1}v_r(\xi),
\]
where \(v_r\) is homogeneous of degree \(r\) in \(\xi\).  After the lower-degree terms have been determined, the degree-\(r\) part of the residual equations is
\[
 J(v_0)v_r=-R_r(\xi,v_1,\ldots,v_{r-1}).                      \tag{11}
\]
The matrix \(J(v_0)\) is invertible by (7), so (11) uniquely determines \(v_r\) for every \(r\).  Hence each of the \(2^d\) displayed points determines a formal section over the entire covariance formal neighborhood.

If \(f\in P_G\), then after any such section is substituted, (8) supplies a supported source lift and therefore
\[
 f(\Sigma^{\star}+\xi)=0
 \quad\text{in }\mathbb C[[\xi]].
\]
Translation by \(\Sigma^{\star}\) is injective on the covariance polynomial ring, because the entries of \(\xi\) are algebraically independent.  It follows that
\[
 P_G=(0),\qquad K_G=\mathbb C(\sigma_{ij}:i\leq j).            \tag{12}
\]
By (10), \(L\) and \(K_G\) have the same transcendence degree \(M_0\).  Since \(L\) is finitely generated over \(K_G\), the extension \(L/K_G\) is finite.  By \(\mathrm{thm:incidence\mbox{-}localization}\), its generic fiber is the integral residual fiber and no directed-coordinate expression has been inverted.

Partition the directed variables into singleton blocks \(A_i=(a_i)\), singleton blocks \(C_i=(c_i)\), and the size-\(d\) block \(Z=(z_1,\ldots,z_d)\).  From the defining formula for \(F_{ij}\), the three residual equations associated with index \(i\) have block degrees bounded respectively by
\[
 A_i+C_i,\qquad A_i+Z,\qquad C_i+Z.
\]
Because \(L/K_G\) is finite and has characteristic zero, its \([L:K_G]\) embeddings give \([L:K_G]\) distinct isolated points of the geometric generic residual fiber: the disturbance coordinates are recovered from \(\Omega=(I_N-\Lambda)^{\mathsf T}\Sigma(I_N-\Lambda)\), so distinct source embeddings cannot have the same directed tuple.  Applying \(\mathrm{lem:multihomogeneous\mbox{-}bezout\mbox{-}isolated\mbox{-}bound}\) therefore yields
\[
 [L:K_G]\leq
 \left[\left(\prod_{i=1}^d A_iC_i\right)Z^d\right]
 \prod_{i=1}^d(A_i+C_i)(A_i+Z)(C_i+Z)=2^d.                    \tag{13}
\]
For each \(i\), exactly two selections in the corresponding three factors produce \(A_iC_iZ\); multiplying these independent choices proves the last equality.

Conversely, each formal section constructed above defines a homomorphism from the integral incidence ring to \(\mathbb C[[\xi]]\), and all these homomorphisms restrict to the same injective covariance translation.  The image contains \(M_0\) algebraically independent translated covariance coordinates.  By (10) and \(R_{\mathrm{inc}}/I_G\cong R_{\mathrm{src}}\) from \(\mathrm{thm:incidence\mbox{-}localization}\), the domain also has dimension \(M_0\).  The prime kernel of each section consequently has height zero; since the domain is integral, that kernel is zero.  Passing to fraction fields gives \(2^d\) embeddings of \(L\) over the common embedded copy of \(K_G\).  Their restrictions to \(K_G(z_1)\) are distinct because their \(z_1\)-series have pairwise distinct constant terms.  It follows that
\[
 2^d\leq[K_G(z_1):K_G]\leq[L:K_G]\leq2^d.                   \tag{14}
\]
Thus
\[
 d_{e^{\star}}(G^{\star}_{k,N})=2^d=2^{k+1}.                 \tag{15}
\]
Characteristic zero makes the minimal polynomial of \(z_1\) separable.  After clearing its coefficient denominators, exclude the zero sets of those denominators and of its nonzero discriminant.  This is a proper algebraic exceptional set, and on its nonempty Zariski-open complement the \(2^d\) roots are distinct.  The affine-coordinate conclusion of \(\mathrm{thm:incidence\mbox{-}localization}\) identifies those roots with exactly the finite queried-coordinate projection.

For \(n>N\), append a new vertex \(w\) that is bidirected with every old vertex, add the directed edge \(0\to w\), and put that edge in \(T\).  No missing residual then involves \(w\).  Let \(x_w=\lambda_{0w}\), let \(s_w\) denote the new covariance row, and write \(L_0,K_0\) and \(L_1,K_1\) for the source and covariance fields before and after this extension.  Conditional on the old source coordinates and \(x_w\), covariance congruence is an invertible triangular polynomial change between the allowed new disturbance row and \(s_w\).  Therefore
\[
 L_1=L_0(x_w,s_w),\qquad K_1=K_0(s_w),                        \tag{16}
\]
where \(x_w\) and the entries of \(s_w\) are algebraically independent over \(L_0\).  The minimal polynomial of \(z_1\) over \(K_0\) remains irreducible over the purely transcendental extension \(K_0(s_w)\): indeed, a factorization over the latter field can be cleared of denominators and common polynomial content; degrees in the indeterminates \(s_w\) add in the resulting polynomial domain, whereas the original polynomial has degree zero in them, so the factors already lie in \(K_0[t]\).  Consequently
\[
 [K_1(z_1):K_1]=[K_0(z_1):K_0]=2^d.                          \tag{17}
\]
Iteration proves (15) for every \(n\geq2k+4\).  Each added edge is a tree edge, so (2) and the excess budget remain valid.  Finally, \(\mathrm{thm:orientation\mbox{-}upper\mbox{-}bound}\) gives \(D_k(n)\leq2^{k+1}\), while the constructed query gives the reverse inequality.  Hence
\[
 D_k(n)=2^{k+1}\qquad(n\geq2k+4),
\]
and the discriminant argument above gives the claimed nonempty Zariski-open set on which the original queried coefficient separates all algebraic branches.

added_lemmas.statement:
For every \(n\geq2\) and every \(k\in\{0,\ldots,(n-1)(n-2)/2\}\),
\[
 D_k(n)=2^{k+1}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad n\geq2k+4.
\]
In particular, throughout the complementary strip \(n<2k+4\), one has the strict inequality \(D_k(n)<2^{k+1}\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Assume first that \(n\geq2k+4\).  Then \(\mathrm{thm:large\mbox{-}size\mbox{-}frontier}\) gives
\[
 D_k(n)=2^{k+1}.                                               \tag{18}
\]
Conversely, suppose \(n<2k+4\).  Set \(N=n-1\) and \(g=k+1\).  The size and index assumptions give \(N\geq1\) and \(g\geq1\), while
\[
 N=n-1<2k+3=2g+1.                                             \tag{19}
\]
The exact maximality characterization in \(\mathrm{lem:joint\mbox{-}orientation\mbox{-}frontier}\) states that \(\vartheta_{N,g}=2^g\) if and only if \(N\geq2g+1\).  Equation (19), together with the universal bound \(\vartheta_{N,g}\leq2^g\) in that lemma, therefore implies
\[
 \vartheta_{n-1,k+1}<2^{k+1}.                                 \tag{20}
\]
Applying \(\mathrm{thm:orientation\mbox{-}upper\mbox{-}bound}\) and then (20) gives
\[
 D_k(n)\leq\vartheta_{n-1,k+1}<2^{k+1}.                       \tag{21}
\]
Thus equality is impossible when \(n<2k+4\), and (18)--(21) prove the equivalence.  The argument establishes strict submaximality in the complementary strip; it does not assert an exact value there.
